moc.chu: According to Hesiod, the lion was raised by Hera and sent to terrorize the hills of Nemea.
Because its golden fur was impervious to attack, it could not be killed with mortal weapons.
The first of Heracles' twelve labours, set by King Eurystheus (his cousin), was to slay the Nemean lion.
He discovered the fur's protective property after the arrow bounced harmlessly off the creature's thigh.
In the dark and close quarters, Heracles stunned the beast with his club.
He eventually killed it by strangling it with his bare hands.
Heracles wore the Nemean lion's coat after killing it.
To celebrate the heroic accomplishment of Heracles' labour, Zeus used the Nemean lion to create the constellation Leo.
